answer: Each account must post a bond that is locked before it can submit work, and a randomly selected peer group audits samples against the task’s stated criteria. If an audit finds fabricated evidence or duplicate identities, the bond is slashed and the account loses access to future rewards; honest auditors earn part of the penalty. A sybil attacker therefore has to tie up real capital across many accounts and risks losing it, while merely making identities wander, carry a lantern, or name themselves raven earns no trust.
